experiment_name: Update-count learnability sweep (0/25/50/100) for BUY_PROPERTY/ACCEPT_TRADE via --reuse-replay, same baseline checkpoint + same existing replay each point

algorithm_config.mode: reuse_replay (--reuse-replay): no new self-play games, no new search, no seed consumed - matches the task instruction not to generate new self-play data
algorithm_config.each_budget_starts_fresh_from: the same baseline_pretraining.pt checkpoint every time (never chained/continued from another budget's output) - input_checkpoint_sha256 verified identical (22ae2abea6...) across all four runs
algorithm_config.single_variable: update budget only - same baseline, same replay buffer, same sampling seed each run. Verified deterministic prefix: the 25-update run's train_stats equal the 50-update run's first 25 entries exactly, and the 50-update run's train_stats equal the 100-update run's first 50 entries exactly (element-wise equality check on loss/policy_loss/value_loss/gradient_norm).
algorithm_config.replay_provenance_caveat: This project's own existing test suite (tests/test_monopolyzero_native_train_candidate.py::test_real_engine_smoke_one_seed_tiny_training_and_checkpoint_roundtrip) writes into this exact default REPLAY_DIR as a side effect of running the tests (it calls train_candidate() without overriding replay_dir). Running that test suite as a pre-flight sanity check (immediately before this sweep) therefore regenerated the on-disk replay via that test's own fixed, deterministic recipe: 1 self-play game, seed=43000, SearchConfig(simulations=4, max_depth=16), max_rounds=5, baseline_pretraining.pt, random/np/torch seeded to 0 - the exact same recipe documented in this script's own commit history as having produced the replay in the first place. Resulting position count (286) matched the pre-existing replay exactly both times this was checked. No new DEV seed was consumed (43000 is already inside the registered 023 seed pool) and no seed/parameter outside this already-fixed, already-committed recipe was used, so this is not new/arbitrary self-play data by the task's intent, but it is not byte-for-byte verified against a hash taken before this session started (no prior hash was ever recorded) - flagged here rather than silently assumed. All four sweep runs below read the exact same on-disk replay (verified identical positions_loaded=286 and identical greedy_selection_before_training across all four runs).

metrics.trend_buy_property: greedy_rate stays 0.0 at 0/25/50 updates and only reaches 1/14 = 7.14% at 100 updates. mean_raw_prior is NOT monotonic: 0.222 (0up) -> 0.141 (25up, a drop) -> 0.186 (50up) -> 0.166 (100up) - never recovers to its 0-update value within this budget. mean_prior_rank improves mildly and mostly monotonically: 2.93 -> 2.71 -> 2.50 -> 2.64 (best at 50up, slightly worse at 100up).
metrics.trend_accept_trade: greedy_rate stays 0.0 at 0/25/50 updates and only reaches 1/40 = 2.5% at 100 updates. mean_raw_prior falls monotonically and never recovers: 0.133 (0up) -> 0.057 (25up) -> 0.075 (50up) -> 0.062 (100up) - lower at 100up than at 0up. mean_prior_rank gets WORSE before it gets better: 6.53 (0up) -> 7.35 (25up, worse) -> 4.85 (50up) -> 4.68 (100up) - net improvement over baseline by 100up but non-monotonic along the way.
metrics.trend_loss: total_loss falls monotonically at every sampled endpoint (2.748 update#1 -> 1.541 @25up final -> 1.315 @50up final -> 1.043 @100up final). value_loss collapses sharply and monotonically (1.335 update#1 -> 0.144 @25up -> 0.032 @50up -> 0.010 @100up) - with only 286 positions and batch_size 32, 100 updates is >11x pass-equivalent exposure to the same fixed dataset, so this reads as the value head overfitting this small fixed replay rather than generalizing. policy_loss falls more modestly (1.413 update#1 -> 1.397 @25up -> 1.283 @50up -> 1.033 @100up) and does not track value_loss's steep drop.

result: Zero ASU modules loaded in any of the four runs (asu_modules_loaded_count=0 every time), zero new self-play games/positions generated by this sweep itself, and input_checkpoint_sha256 confirmed identical (baseline, not chained) across all four points. Training over this replay DOES measurably move BUY_PROPERTY/ACCEPT_TRADE prior mass and rank away from their 0-update baseline within 100 updates, but the movement is small, non-monotonic, and mostly does NOT flip the greedy (argmax) decision: greedy_rate for both actions stays exactly 0.0 at 0/25/50 updates and only reaches 1 of 14 BUY_PROPERTY opportunities (7.1%) and 1 of 40 ACCEPT_TRADE opportunities (2.5%) by 100 updates. Raw prior mass for both actions is LOWER at 100 updates than at 0 updates (BUY_PROPERTY 0.222->0.166, ACCEPT_TRADE 0.133->0.062), and BUY_PROPERTY's own prior dips before partially recovering (0.222->0.141->0.186->0.166) rather than moving toward the target action in a clean trend. Meanwhile value_loss collapses to near-zero (1.335->0.010) far faster than policy_loss falls (1.413->1.033), on a replay of only 286 positions with batch_size 32 - a classic small-fixed-dataset overfitting signature on the value head, not evidence of the policy head robustly learning BUY_PROPERTY/ACCEPT_TRADE as target actions. Given the very small sample (only 14 BUY_PROPERTY and 40 ACCEPT_TRADE opportunities total, from a single short self-play game), a single greedy flip in each category is weak, low-power evidence and cannot by itself support either a GO or a KILL conclusion about whether native ASU-free MCTS/self-play targets can teach these two actions - the honest read is: some prior movement is visible, but it is small, non-monotonic, mostly below the greedy-decision threshold, and measured on a dataset too small to be conclusive. A larger self-play replay (more seeds, more positions) is needed before this question can be answered with adequate statistical power - not run here per this task's explicit scope (no new self-play data, no large strength evaluation).
notes: seeds is null (not [43000]) because --reuse-replay mode does not consume/validate any seed - the replay's own generating seed is a property of the replay (see algorithm_config.replay_provenance_caveat), not of this sweep's own commands. Trained candidate checkpoints (updates_{0,25,50,100}.pt, ~3.9MB each) are NOT committed per CLAUDE.md - referenced by SHA-256 and local path (artifacts/monopolyzero_native_train_candidate/sweep/) only. The four --output JSON payloads (small, a few KB to ~20KB each) are committed under docs/baseline_runs/ per this project's convention for small structured result payloads. runtime.wall_time_s is the sum of all four runs' elapsed_s; runtime.peak_rss_gib is the max across the four (each run measured independently, not a single shared process).
